prose.title: CBP Did Nothing for Three Months, Then Spent to the Last Dollar
prose.dek: Derrick Whitman started April with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players and made no move until the auction, then spent {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}} on Jonathan Taylor, Kyle Pitts and the Tony Pollard that C-Town let go. He has {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of cap room left, and the preseason simulation ranks CBP {{f.team.0002.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was nearly empty: {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0002.cap_opening}} in salary. Nico Collins was the one top-twelve starter, and Jordan Love, Emeka Egbuka and Garrett Wilson were solid. The {{f.team.0002.holes_opening}} holes were Keaton Mitchell at running back, nobody at all at the second running back spot, Cole Kmet at tight end, Ricky Pearsall in a flex and Spencer Rattler in the superflex.

Then Whitman did nothing, which is how he works: the roster business happens in silence. No trade, no cut, no extension before the rookie draft, and his one expiring rookie deal, A.T. Perry's, simply ran out.

t.0002.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft was the whole pre-auction offseason. Whitman made {{f.team.0002.rookie_picks_count}} picks, two in the first round: Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08, a slot where history finds a usable player a little under half the time, and Eli Stowers at 1.12. Jonah Coleman at 2.01, Ted Hurst, Cade Klubnik and Keyshaun Elliott followed. Sadiq and Coleman are already on the redraft board, both replacement-level for now.

No Expired Rookie Auction buys, no tags, no cuts, no trades. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0002.cap_preauction}} committed: plenty of room, and plenty of rebuilding to do with it.

He opened a little more first. Jordan Love was extended and restructured on the auction's opening weekend, {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_salary}} this year cut to {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_salary_2}}, and then Whitman bought a backfield. Jonathan Taylor cost {{f.team.0002.faa_14802_price}}, D'Andre Swift {{f.team.0002.faa_14797_price}}, and Tony Pollard, cut by C-Town on lock day, {{f.team.0002.faa_14085_price}} after thirteen bids. Kyle Pitts cost {{f.team.0002.faa_15329_price}}. In all it came to {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}} for {{f.team.0002.faa_lots_won}} players.

What it bought was real: Taylor is an Elite RB1, Pitts a High-end TE1, Swift the Good buy, with Pollard, Aaron Jones and Michael Pittman as depth. His offense gained more than all but one other at the auction, {{f.team.0002.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}, and ranked {{f.team.0002.faa_off_rank|ord}} for what each dollar added.

The contracts that followed ran him right to the cap. Pitts signed a front-loaded deal, {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_tcv}} in all. In late August Nico Collins's deal was restructured and put straight back, a temporary {{f.team.0002.restructure_room_freed}} of room, and the next day Whitman took Jayden Reed, three depth players and {{f.team.0002.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money from Blake Bombers for Pearsall, Coleman and a 2027 fourth. He cut Kmet at no cost, claimed Calvin Ridley and Xavier Hutchinson off waivers, and sits at {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0002.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Taylor, Collins and Pitts, five solid ones around them, and {{f.team.0002.holes_today}} hole, Pollard in a flex. Quarterback is the soft spot: Tyler Shough and Love both grade as a Mid QB2, and his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0002.qb_rank|ord}} in the league. The kicker and the defense are footnotes.

captions.t.0002.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Whitman has the best career all-play record in the league, {{f.team.0002.hist_allplay_pct}}, across {{f.team.0002.hist_seasons}} seasons in two spells since {{f.team.0002.hist_first_season}}. His teams have had the league's best all-play record {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_titles}} times, in {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_title_years}}, and won {{f.team.0002.hist_div_titles}} division titles, but the championship count is one, in {{f.team.0002.hist_title_years}}, with a runner-up finish in {{f.team.0002.hist_runner_up_years}}.

LEGION OF BOOM has the league's most decorated owner in Shawn Blake, and the simulation ranks his Bombers {{f.league.power_rank_0010|ord}} in the league, Gride {{f.league.power_rank_0003|ord}}, and CBP {{f.team.0002.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0002.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and a {{f.team.0002.sim_p_division}} chance at the division. Whitman plays Blake and Gerardi five times each.

The next three years, CBP style, no commas. 2027 CBP makes the playoffs and does not say a word about it until somebody else brings it up and then CBP says a lot. 2028 the quarterback problem gets solved in silence at an auction and the all-play record goes up again. 2029 a second title and CBP thanks the whole league because we are all friends here and then goes quiet for a year.
Week one has barely touched CBP: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Leonard Williams had a sack and CBP has {{f.team.0002.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
